historical_references.reference: Arjuna, a central character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, was also known as Arjuna, or Arjraj. He was the third of the five Pandava brothers and was considered one of the greatest warriors in Hindu mythology. Arjuna's mentor was the god Bhagavan Krishna, who advised him on the righteous path and helped him overcome his inner demons.

Another reference to Arjuna can be found in the Puranas, particularly the Bhagavata Purana. In this text, Arjuna is described as the divine warrior who was chosen by Lord Vishnu to fight the demon Narakasura. During this battle, Arjuna was granted the divine weapon Pashupata Astra, which was capable of destroying all demons and evil beings.
